maya: Heads up — hit a correctness edge while testing a conditional-evict flag on shared-prefix flows.

sam: details? reproduction steps?

maya: repro is small. Two tenants share a prefix in the same slab. We flip `conditional_evict=true` to speed hotset churn. Observed reads returning stale values for ~200ms after a handoff.

noah: that sounds like a handshake race between demote and the eviction marker write. Did you see any lease/epoch mismatches in logs?

maya: logs show: demote request -> write tombstone marker -> lease transfer ack -> read hits old KV before tombstone fully compacted. Sequence looks like tombstone was visible but the in-memory residency not updated atomically.

li: can you paste the small log snippet?

maya: ```
[11:02:13.123] demote prefix/x slab=3 token=7 -> write tombstone id=tx-444
[11:02:13.125] lease transfer ack tenant=B epoch=102
[11:02:13.320] read tenant=B prefix/x -> returned old-value v1 (expected tombstone)
```

sam: hmm. 200ms gap. Are we flushing an async compaction task? Maybe tombstone enqueued but compaction that clears residency is delayed.

noah: two hypotheses: 1) tombstone is durable but residency map update is racy across threads, 2) read path can consult fallback store (shadow read) before eviction finishes.

maya: I believe #1. The code currently updates slab residency after ack from storage, but the ack path runs on a different executor. If the reader checks residency before the executor runs, it sees stale residency -> returns old value.

li: agreed. Proposed short fixes: a) make the write+tombstone+residency update an ordered pipeline (blocking) for shared prefixes, b) introduce a soft-lease where readers check tombstone epoch and reject reads pre-epoch, c) emit a demote-inflight marker that readers consult.

sam: tradeoffs: (a) increases tail latency for demotes; (b) adds complexity to read fast-path with epoch checks; (c) is a light-weight gate but requires extra checks on every read.

noah: also consider service-level option: `conditional_evict_strict=true` only on Dedicated where latency SLOs can absorb demote stall. For hosted, default to async but with best-effort read fencing.

maya: i sketched a small change: on tombstone write, also publish an in-memory fence token into a lock-free ring that readers consult quickly (cheap read path check). If token present, readers block briefly or fallback to secondary read.

li: can you drop the sketch here?

maya: ```
// pseudo
write_tombstone(prefix) -> storage.persist(tombstone) then publish(fence_token(prefix, epoch)) on executor
read(prefix) {
  token = fence_ring.peek(prefix)
  if token && token.epoch >= read_epoch {
    // either block-spin short or fallback to shadow-store read
  }
  return fast_read(prefix)
}
```

sam: I like fence_ring idea. Needs correctness proof: ensure token publication happens-before any reader observing tombstone. That means the writer must publish token on the same memory ordering as the storage ack. If ack is remote, we must still guarantee ordering.

noah: also test: multi-node handoff where slab migrates — readers on other nodes must get the fence signal. Otherwise you still see stale reads.

maya: true. For cross-node we'd propagate a transient lease/epoch bump in the handoff protocol. Handoff ack includes new epoch; readers compare local epoch and, if behind, trigger lease-sync.

li: plan proposal: 1) short-term: add fence_ring and local reader check -> reduces local races; 2) mid-term: extend handoff protocol to carry epoch fence and a small RPC to N-1 nodes for hot prefixes; 3) long-term: formalize demote atomicity contract in the prefix ownership RFC.

sam: +1 for phased approach. Also add unit/integration tests: tight-loop reads across handoff with injected executors yielding.

maya: I'll draft a tiny spike PR for fence_ring and a sim test that reproduces the 200ms gap. Will also include a flag `conditional_evict_local_fence=true`.

li: noted. Also add an observability event: emit demote->fence publish latency metric so we can see the window shrink.
